transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Investigators are working to determine a motive behind the shooting yesterday at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon.
A 16-year-old gunman opened fire, killing three children and one teacher.
An armed bystander later shot and killed the suspect.
Joni Auden-Lan from Oregon Public Broadcasting reports authorities are trying to piece together the circumstances leading up to the attack.
We just know that soon after the shooter entered the school by shooting off the locks on the doors,
this bystander followed them and at some point within the next couple of minutes gunned them down themselves.
We still don't know who this person is or, again, why they were at the school.
A seven-year-old student and teacher are hospitalized in critical condition.
Authorities are planning to hold a press briefing later today.
Young Americans were a key part of President Trump's winning coalition in 2024.
But nearly two years later, that support may be fading.
Left-leaning polling from firm Navigator Research talked to eight Trump supporters.
And as NPR's Elena Moore reports, some of those Gen Z'ers say they feel disenfranchised.
Trump campaigned on lowering costs, but as prices remain high, some Gen Z supporters have reached a breaking point.
I just feel like nothing went correctly. I just feel like everything got worse.
That's Jon in Florida.
He agreed to be part of the focus group on condition that he would only be identified by his first name.
After voting for Trump since 2016, he's planning on backing Democrats this year.
Not everyone went as far. Several participants said they would still vote for Republicans.
But others also highlighted another challenge for Democrats and Republicans right now,
saying they've grown distrustful of both sides.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
Emergency crews in Southern California are working against strong winds to contain a number of wildfires.
Steve Fetterman reports a blaze in Malibu has grown to about 200 acres.
Overnight, the Santana winds did significantly die down, giving firefighters a chance to go after hot spots.
The Bryson fire, as it's being called, was first detected in the late afternoon.
Around 100 homes are in danger. Evacuation orders are in effect.
During the night, water-dropping helicopters were used.
Now, the winds are expected to increase later today.
The red flag alert issued by the National Weather Service will continue until tomorrow.
Meanwhile, another fire has been burning to the south near Camp Pendleton.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Fetterman in Malibu, California.
Stocks are trading mixed on Wall Street at this hour.
The Dow was up 44 points. This is NPR News.
The number of people facing life-threatening hunger has doubled over the past decade.
That's according to a new analysis.
NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports food crises in just three countries account for much of that toll.
266 million people worldwide are facing acute hunger, according to a report from the nonprofit Action Against Hunger.
About a third of them live in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Sudan, and Nigeria.
Conflict is a major cause of the crisis. Ongoing fighting is displacing millions of people while making it harder to deliver humanitarian aid.
Climate change is playing a role, too, with disasters destroying crops and livelihoods.
And rising poverty in some countries is putting food out of reach for many.
This increase in hunger is happening as funds to fight it drop.
Humanitarian aid targeting food insecurity fell by nearly 60 percent over the past few years.
The authors say that peace and more funding are needed to reverse the trend.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Teenagers demanding more resources for schools in France continue to clash with police.
Many have been arrested or injured during the protests.
Police are facing criticism over weapons described as non-lethal that have caused serious injuries.
A police union has also filed a complaint against the state, saying officers have been put in danger.
Investigations into alleged police misconduct are growing as President Emmanuel Macron approaches the end of his term in May.
I'm Windsor Johnston, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Gunman kills three children and a teacher at Bend, Oregon elementary school; bystander shoots suspect dead
Investigators still seeking motive in Bend, Oregon school shooting; two students and teacher hospitalized
Young male Trump supporters in focus group voice disillusionment over high prices, with some planning to back Democrats
Wildfire in Malibu, California grows to about 200 acres as Santana winds die down overnight
Stocks trade mixed on Wall Street, with the Dow up 44 points
Number of people facing life-threatening hunger doubles over past decade, led by Congo, Sudan, and Nigeria
French teenagers protesting school funding clash with police; police criticized over injurious non-lethal weapons
